clue.text: A marine detachment

parts.note: reads like a squad of Royal Marines, but means a piece of land cut off from the rest by the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A small island is literally land detached and surrounded by sea, so it is a detachment in the marine setting.

clue.text: In moral tale, rejection of evil held to be faultless

indicators.note: held means one piece is gripped inside the other, here the turned word sits within the story

parts.note: a fable is a short story with a moral

indicators.note: rejection of means the word for evil is turned back, read from right to left

parts.note: ill can mean evil or harm

explanation.surface: Someone praises a moralising story in which evil is rejected as perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word at the start, but it supplies its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Infallible means incapable of error, so never at fault.

clue.text: Grim slum centre purged

indicators.note: centre picks the two middle letters of the word slum

parts.note: purged of something means rid of it

explanation.surface: A bleak slum district has been cleared out.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid can mean gruesome or shocking, close to grim in describing horrible details.

clue.text: Bouncy activity here in late romp, maybe?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the words in late romp are just one possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A frolic late at night might involve a lot of bouncing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals rearranging INLATEROMP; the definition 'Bouncy activity here' points to the place where people bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: A springy sheet on which people jump is the place where bouncing happens.

clue.text: Come to conclusion lies are involved

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters of lies are become tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone works out that lies have been told.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to grasp or understand it, reaching a conclusion about it.

clue.text: A limit one treated with special reserve

indicators.note: treated means the letters are processed and worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone has a limit dealt with by a special reserve fund.
explanation.walkthrough: The British Special Reserve, formed in 1908, was the successor to the old militia, a body of part-time citizen soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen army held back for emergencies is a reserve force of non-professional soldiers.

clue.text: One having new development in gold

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters are placed inside the word for gold

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: development suggests the letters of new grow into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A person with a fresh development in gold mining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One having' is a terse definition: the person who has something.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessor is someone who has something, so 'one having' describes it.

clue.text: National I disparage, with sound sense?

indicators.note: with sound sense hints that the phrase is to be heard rather than read, its sound giving the answer

parts.note: to disparage is to slander, so I disparage is I slander

explanation.surface: Someone admits belittling others, but claims to do so sensibly.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'I slander' matches a citizen of a North Atlantic island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, here a citizen of Iceland.

clue.text: True, it's not quite happening

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: a happening is an event or occurrence

explanation.surface: Someone concedes a report is true but the thing has not quite happened.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and true both describe something level, straight or aligned.

clue.text: Spice ale liberally to make it noteworthy

indicators.note: liberally suggests freely mixing the letters of spice ale into a new order

explanation.surface: A brewer adds plenty of spice to beer to make it special.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial means exceptional or particular, so outstanding enough to be noteworthy.

clue.text: Counter of many trees — every one!

parts.note: a forest is a large area covered with many trees
every one is all of them

explanation.surface: Someone counts trees in a wood, every last one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To counter a move is to prevent it in advance, thwarting it.

clue.text: Girl given direction into French resort

indicators.note: into means the letter for a direction is placed inside the resort name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A young woman is given directions to a resort in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative who is the daughter of one's sibling is a girl in the family.

clue.text: Shelf not quite big enough for the accounts book

indicators.note: not quite big enough means the word is one letter short, missing its end

parts.note: a ledger is the book in which accounts are kept

explanation.surface: A shelf is a little too small to hold the account book.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow horizontal projection from a wall is a shelf.

clue.text: Domestic is a novice following orderly sequence, we hear

indicators.note: following means the letters for a and novice come after the spoken phrase
we hear means the phrase is to be heard, its sound standing for a similar-sounding word

parts.note: in turn means one after another in proper sequence
L is a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A housemaid is a beginner who follows a set routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes IN TURN sound like INTERN; then A and L (learner) follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic means home or inside the country, the opposite of foreign or external.

clue.text: On the whole the bird has to be quite fast

parts.note: the whole is all of it
an egret is a type of heron
taken as written

explanation.surface: Overall, the bird has to be fairly fast.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the tempo marking means moderately brisk, a little slower than allegro.

clue.text: Worship that is on solid ground

indicators.note: on here means the abbreviation is laid on either side of the reworked word

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: ground means the letters of solid are crushed and broken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone worships while standing on firm earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a loose container signal here: the abbreviation is spread over the reworked word, its letters at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone excessively is to worship them like a deity.

clue.text: Begin to speak out when I have a drink inside

indicators.note: inside means the two pieces go within the word for speaking out

parts.note: to orate is to speak out in a formal way
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone starts making a speech once they have had a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' and 'have' are only link words joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To start or arise is to begin, coming into being.

clue.text: English public school rule Dan breaks

indicators.note: breaks means the letters of rule Dan are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A pupil named Dan defies the rules at a private school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public school' is an old fee-paying private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Arundel is a West Sussex town, here named as the seat of a fee-paying school.

clue.text: Befuddled, he ended up penniless — ignored

indicators.note: befuddled means confused, so the letters are mixed into a new order
penniless means without a P, the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A drunk man found himself broke and disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penniless' removes P from HE ENDED UP, leaving HEENDEDU; 'Befuddled' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disregarded has not been heeded, so it was paid no attention.

clue.text: I'd allow, somehow, having been floored

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of I'd allow reach the result in some unspecified way

explanation.surface: A boxer grudgingly admits being knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: Being laid low means knocked down or incapacitated, just as being floored is.

clue.text: For wrong-doing, we get bird!

indicators.note: wrong suggests the following letters are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: For their misdeeds, the culprits get a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get bird' is British slang for serving jail time, which disguises the definition; 'wrong' rearranges DOINGWE.
explanation.definitionFit: This wild duck is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Overthrow from power one Arab linked to an international organisation?

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A deposed Arab ruler appeals to a world body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' looks like a person but is the horse breed, as the question mark warns.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone from their mount is to topple them, and figuratively to oust them from authority.

clue.text: Ineffective way to economise

definitions.meaning: achieving nothing, of no practical value
consuming a smaller amount is a means of saving money

explanation.definitionFit: Futile things are of no practical value, and read as two words the answer is advice to consume a smaller amount.

clue.text: Infernal place to stay — get them out of it!

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, Hell
to lodge is to stay somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a hellish guesthouse urges others to be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To force people out of a place is to remove or eject them.

clue.text: Wobbly solo flight has grave ending

indicators.note: flight suggests the letters of solo fly off and land in a new order
ending picks the last letter of the word grave

explanation.surface: A pilot's first solo flight ends in a crash and burial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' rearranges SOLO to LOOS, and E comes from 'grave ending'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loose is not firmly fixed, so it wobbles.

clue.text: Fear losing head and a boob

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word for fear is dropped

parts.note: terror is extreme fear

explanation.surface: Someone panics after making a gaffe.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is British slang for a blunder or mistake.

clue.text: As a rule, give up second outing

indicators.note: outing means the letter for second is put out of the word

parts.note: to resign is to give up a post

explanation.surface: Usually, a failed candidate gives up after a second attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as a monarch.

clue.text: Narrative content of some picture-books

indicators.note: content of means the letters are found inside the following words, the contents they hold

explanation.surface: Some illustrated children's books contain a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A long heroic poem or saga is a narrative.

clue.text: Where hammers make music

parts.note: suggests a forge or workshop, but means the instrument whose felt hammers strike strings

explanation.definitionFit: Inside this keyboard instrument, felt-tipped hammers strike strings to produce notes.

clue.text: This interpreter, a banker, gets it wrong

parts.note: a banker is a river, which has banks; the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of gets it are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A bank employee mistranslates a passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword slang for a river, because it has banks; here the Exe in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An exegetist explains and interprets texts, especially scripture.

clue.text: Smart, to the point of genius, perhaps

parts.note: smart means clever
a ness is a headland or promontory, a point of land

explanation.surface: Someone is so smart it borders on brilliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Genius is an extreme instance of intelligence, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: A fund only partly open

indicators.note: only partly means just part of the following words is used, the letters lying within them

explanation.surface: A fund is only partly accessible to investors.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a fastening or package is to open it.
